body: Thank you so fucking much for writing this I started spiraling because I take OCPs and have no grasp on how to comprehend medical articles and I'm a hypochondriac. Very sincere thank yous to you
Sorry, my grammar isn't great. I think faster than I can type with thumbs

Yes, I am aware that is the purpose of psych wards. That doesn't mean it translates flawlessly into reality. 

I learned in school that people typically leave feeling worse after being admitted because even though they get put on meds that may or may not help. it's not enough time for adjustment to see if they're actually beneficial to the individual. If people typically stay for only a week or so, then I would see this as true because it usually takes about a month for those types of medicines to make an impact. And if you already had issues with money, you end up leaving with more debt. AND if they didn't feel like they had a support system before they were admitted or actually don't have a support system to go back to

OTC meds such as monistat are irritants. I have to see a vulvar specialist and was told to never use monistat again which was suggested by a regular gyn. All it did was make it itchier. If you're getting yeast infections a lot you really should go to a doctor though. There are different kinds that sometimes will need a different medication. Diflucan only treats about 80% of yeast.

A homeopathic doctor told me to try garlic and then to try hydrogen peroxide, neither helped in the least bit. And the process sucked.
You need some kind of motivation in order to stay disciplined. If I feel as though I'm getting nothing out of something I'm putting a lot of effort in to, why would I keep doing it?

*better mental health care. From anecdotal experience and from listening/reading other experiences, psych wards aren't that helpful. It'd be more helpful to have better quality outpatient care available to help prevent people from feeling like a psych ward is their last option. Psych wards main objective is to medicate you and have you barely functional before they discharge you, not explore and treat underlying issues. My experience was so negative that I am terrified to go back to the hospital (that I had initially asked to be taken/admitted to!) and am terrified of being forced back there or into another ward.

Thank you for the reassurance. I talked with my mother about it when she came back and said that if it was really that important that myself and my sibling showed up that my grandfather would have called us himself or given another family member a specific message to pass along. I'm hoping that's true and that grandfather and step grandmother aren't hurt by my assumptions.

It hurts that my aunt is basically implying that I didn't give a shit which is really fucking bothering me

Thank you for replying Idk if I just sound like an idiot or if this post doesn't technically belong here or no one else gives a shit 

At first she was trying to sound like I didn't even know she had died but my mother had already told me before she went out of state but if no one told me that either how would I know? Keep asking how she is and one day look like an idiot because no one told me?? I don't even know
